subject: Residency, retention, and deletion checkpoints for evaluation
messages:
From: Liam Carter <liam.carter@greenwayhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency and deletion checkpoints for evaluation

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. As we prepare our security review, we need a concise Q&A to share with our legal and engineering teams about where Greenway data would be processed and how it is retained / deleted. Can you confirm the following for your hosted API and dedicated options?

- Primary regions where inference executes (hosted default and Dedicated capability).
- List of subprocessors that touch runtime requests / caching / logging and their primary regions.
- Whether request payloads or model context are written to disk (ephemeral vs persistent).
- Default retention for request logs, usage metrics, and any model KV caches.
- Process & SLA for a full customer data purge (account decommission or regulatory takedown).

Also, please attach any evidence (subprocessor inventory, residency map, SOC2 summary) we can forward to procurement. We prefer short bullet answers so our reviewers can sign off quickly.

Best,
Liam Carter
CTO, Greenway Health
liam.carter@greenwayhealth.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@greenwayhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency and deletion checkpoints for evaluation

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below for your security/eng review; attaching a residency diagram and our subprocessor inventory. Marissa is CC'd if you want a technical walkthrough.

- Primary regions: Hosted API: US (us-east-1) and EU (europe-west-1) active. Dedicated: customers can reserve pools in us-east-1, us-west-2, europe-west-1 or run in a private VPC/On‑Prem package.

- Subprocessors (touching runtime requests or telemetry):
  * CloudInfraCo (compute) — primary regions: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1
  * EdgeCache Inc (transient CDN/KV acceleration) — global PoPs, no persistent storage
  * MetricsCorp (telemetry/logs) — us-central, eu-west-1 (logs forwarded via TLS, see inventory)
  * KeySafe KMS (key management) — regional KMS endpoints (customer-managed option available)

- Disk vs memory for requests:
  * In hosted mode: request payloads and model context are processed in-memory. We do not write request-level context to persistent disk except for developer opt-in audit logs (explicit setting). Ephemeral KV caches are memory-first and kept in RAM-backed instances; they are paged only in emergency and encrypted at rest if persisted.

- Default retention windows:
  * Request logs (audit-level): 30 days by default, configurable up to 365 via contract for enterprise plans.
  * Usage metrics (aggregated): retained 13 months for billing/analytics.
  * KV cache / model context: ephemeral; TTLs are short (default 30s–120s) and not considered customer data storage.

- Customer data purge:
  * Account-level purge: we remove request logs, aggregated metrics, and any persisted artifacts within 72 hours of an approved decommission request.
  * For Dedicated/Private deployments: we provide a documented purge playbook and can coordinate on-site or remote verification.

Attachments: residency-diagram.pdf, subprocessor-inventory.csv, soc2-summary.pdf (high level).

If you want an explicit statement for procurement (export controls / cross-border transfer language), Marissa and I can provide tailored wording — and I will loop our security lead for any cryptographic or evidence specifics.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai

From: Liam Carter <liam.carter@greenwayhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency and deletion checkpoints for evaluation

Evelyn — thanks, that helps a lot. Two follow-ups from our engineering team:

1) Can you confirm whether ephemeral KV caches (used for prefix caching / latency) are ever paged to disk under high-memory pressure? If yes, are those pages encrypted and included in the purge flow?

2) For the 72-hour purge SLA — does that include all backups and snapshot chains (e.g., cloud provider snapshots) or just application-level artifacts? We need to understand timeline for complete removal from backups or to get a reasonable exception template.

If it's easier to have Jonas chime in on cryptography/backups, happy to have him added.

Thanks — Liam

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@greenwayhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency and deletion checkpoints for evaluation

Hi Liam — looping Jonas (security) and adding more precision below.

On KV cache paging and encryption:
- Operational behavior: KV caches are resident in RAM by design. Under extreme memory pressure, our runtime will attempt to shed cache entries; in rare cases we may page memory to local NVMe swap on dedicated hosts for process stability.
- Encryption & purge: Any persisted swap pages are encrypted at rest using customer or provider KMS depending on deployment. Those pages are included in our purge plan — we run targeted zeroing and coordinate with the cloud provider to expire snapshots that contain customer identifiers.

On backups & snapshots and the 72-hour SLA:
- The 72-hour SLA covers application-level deletion of request logs, customer artifacts, and any persisted runtime artifacts we control.
- Cloud provider managed backups/snapshots that are outside our direct control may have their own retention windows; we maintain documented procedures to identify and expire or rotate snapshots containing customer data and will coordinate with you on timelines. For enterprise contracts, we can add explicit snapshot expiration guarantees or a transfer-to-customer process for full on-prem deletion.

Jonas (copied) — a two-sentence confirmation for Liam on encryption defaults and snapshot coordination would be great.

Thanks,
Evelyn

----- Forwarded message from Jonas Weber -----
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@greenwayhealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 13:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency and deletion checkpoints for evaluation

Liam — quick note from security: all persisted runtime artifacts (including any swap or spilled pages) are encrypted with AES-256 using KMS-managed keys by default. For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys and HSM integrations.

We operate a snapshot identification workflow: when a purge is requested, we run an automated scan for snapshots containing customer IDs and either request expiration from the cloud provider or rotate keys so that older snapshots are cryptographically inaccessible. We will add contractual language for snapshot expiration in the SOW if you need a hard SLA.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through the evidence pack.

— Jonas Weber
Director, Security — Redwood Inference
